name: Creep and fatigue of lead (bulging lights, cracked sheet)
describes: Lead is soft and creeps under its own weight and the glass's; its thermal movement is large (29 x 10^-6 /K). A leaded light slowly sags and bows between its saddle bars, the came's leaves loosen and the cement falls out; sheet lead restrained by too many fixings cracks by fatigue at its thin points. The time scale varies enormously: the '100 years or so' said of came is a myth; some leading has failed within years and some has served for more than 800.

cameLifespan.text: The common claim of a lifespan of '100 years or so' is a myth: some leadwork 'disintegrated within years', other came remains 'fully functioning after more than 800 years'.
cameLifespan.source: S. Strobl, 'Lead in Stained Glass Windows', Historic Churches (2002), via The Building Conservation Directory, https://www.buildingconservation.com/articles/leadstainedglass/lead_stained_glass.htm

thermalMovement.conditions: per metre of sheet over a 50 K swing

fixing.text: Sheet lead is fixed at the head of each bay so it can move; that is what keeps it from fatigue cracking.
fixing.source: The Lead Lads, 'Leadwork: the ultimate guide to lead roofing' (BS EN 12588; BS 6915:2001+A1:2014), https://theleadlads.co.uk/leadwork-the-ultimate-guide-to-lead-roofing/
